cards.text: Solomon, son of David, is king over Israel, and the queen of Sheba has just headed home (2 Chronicles 9:12). Now the record turns to his gold, and friend, every single year 666 talents of it come in. Somebody once bought ME for 25 cents.

cards.question: Solomon's 666 talents of gold a year include everything the merchants and traders bring in.

cards.text: Nope, that's EXTRA, and the Arabian kings and governors of the land bring him gold and silver on top of it. Everybody else opens the mail and finds bills. Solomon opens the mail and finds GOLD.
So what do you do with that much gold? Solomon makes 200 large shields of hammered gold, with 600 shekels of gold in each one.

cards.question: Solomon also makes 300 small shields of hammered gold. Where does he put the small gold shields?

answers.text: The House of the Forest of Lebanon

cards.text: Next, Solomon makes a great throne of ivory overlaid with pure gold, with six steps and a gold footstool attached. Beside each armrest stands a lion, and here I was thinking my little gold base was FANCY.

cards.question: Solomon's throne has six steps, with a lion standing at either end of each step. How many lions stand on the steps?
The writer says nothing like Solomon's throne had ever been made for any kingdom.

cards.text: Every drinking cup Solomon owns is gold, and so is every utensil in the House of the Forest of Lebanon. Friend, you could NOT find a plain spoon in that place if you tried.

cards.question: With gold everywhere in Solomon's day, silver was accounted as ___.

cards.text: So how does all this treasure keep showing up? Solomon has the ships of Tarshish, sailing with the servants of Hiram, king of Tyre (2 Chronicles 2:3), and they come back loaded with gold, silver, ivory, apes and peacocks.

cards.question: How often do Solomon's ships of Tarshish come back loaded?

cards.text: Add it all up, and King Solomon surpasses all the kings of the earth in riches AND wisdom. Every other king on the planet is playing for second place.

cards.question: All the kings of the earth seek an audience with Solomon. Why?

answers.text: To hear the wisdom God put in his heart
To see his famous gold shields up close
To ask him for a share of all his gold

cards.question: The visitors who come to hear Solomon show up empty-handed.

cards.text: Year after year, every visitor brings tribute: silver and gold, clothing, weapons, spices, horses and mules. When a scared can opener slid into my old junk drawer, all it brought was NERVES.

cards.question: Solomon has 4,000 stalls for horses and chariots, and 12,000 horses. Where does he station them?

answers.text: In the chariot cities and Jerusalem
Up in the hill country of Ephraim

cards.text: And his rule reaches far. Solomon reigns over all the kings from the Euphrates to the land of the Philistines, as far as the border of Egypt.

cards.question: Remember how silver counted for nothing? In Jerusalem, Solomon makes silver as common as ___.

cards.text: And cedar is as abundant as sycamore in the foothills. Friend, back in my old junk drawer, the only thing that common was DUST.

cards.question: All of Solomon's horses come from inside Israel.

cards.text: Nope, Solomon's horses are imported from Egypt and from all the lands. This man's stables have an INTERNATIONAL guest list.

The rest of Solomon's acts are written in the records of Nathan the prophet, the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite and the visions of Iddo the seer. Iddo's visions also concern Jeroboam son of Nebat, a man who served Solomon (1 Kings 11:26).

cards.question: How long does Solomon reign in Jerusalem over all Israel?

cards.text: And after all that gold and all that wisdom, Solomon rests with his fathers. He's buried in the city of his father David.

findings.problem: The opening identifies Solomon as David's son and as king over Israel, but its verse field cites only 2 Chronicles 9:13, which establishes neither fact. Unlike the queen of Sheba context, these identifications have no supporting reference.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The inventories in 2 Chronicles 9:13-21 and 9:25-28 are mostly detail with little action, yet the walkthrough goes through them item by item and quizzes their numbers and details. Stop 1 is also devoted entirely to the first inventory. These stretches should be summarized within stops rather than receiving their own stop and numerous choice cards.

rule.text: If a stretch is mostly detail and not much happens, it counts. The rule: Papa Dorin sums up the stretch in one story card. A stretch never gets a stop of its own. A long stretch never gets a choice card.

findings.problem: The correct answer uses biblical language about hearing the wisdom God put in Solomon's heart, while both distractors use casual modern phrasing about seeing shields up close and getting a share of gold. The right answer sounds more scriptural and stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
